summary: Alexander Robertson was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (M.A. ~1894–1898) and the University of Glasgow, and served as a missionary with the United Free Church of Scotland (1902–1937).

Alexander Rogers worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College (~1843–1845) and served in the Indian Civil Service from 1845 to 1879.

Alexander Rödel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned a Master of Science by Research at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2008), where he studied under supervisors Steven Sutcliffe and Jeanne Openshaw.

Alexander Schiller works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Appalachian State University (B.A. 2010–2014), UC San Diego (MASIA 2019–2021), and Kansas State University (PhD 2025). He joined the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter (attested 2026).
Alexander Studholme is a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin between ~1996 and 2000.

Alexander W. Macdonald was a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1988), the Musée de l'Homme (attested 1972), Paris Nanterre University as Professor (~1975–1990), and the University of Paris as Editorial Consultant (attested 1982).
Alexander Walker worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of St Andrews (~1778–1780) and held a post with the East India Company from ~1780 to 1812.

Alexander Wynne works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Paul Williams and Rupert Gethin at the University of Bristol (~1996–1999) and completed a DPhil at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich (2000–2003), later serving as a JRF at St John's College, Oxford (2002–2006).

Alexander Yiannopoulos works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and under teachers including Karin Myers, Sherab Sangpo, Khenpo Sherab Dorje, Georges B. J. Dreyfus, Tom Tillemans, John J. Makransky, William S. Waldron, Jay L. Garfield, Douglas S. Duckworth, and Sara L. McClintock.

Alexander Zieseniss was an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg, Freiburg, Hamburg (PhD ~1925–1928), Tübingen, and Berlin, under Carl Bezold, Bruno Liebich, Ernst Leumann, and Walther Schubring. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Breslau (~1934–1945) and completed his Habilitation at Hamburg (1936–1941).

Alexander von Humboldt worked in history/archaeology and other fields. He studied at European University Viadrina (1787), Göttingen (~1789–1790), Jena (~1789), Handelsakademie Hamburg (~1790–1791), and TU Bergakademie Freiberg (~1791–1792), under Georg Forster, Christian Gottlob Heyne, and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, and held a post at Jena.

Alexander von Rospatt is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of London and the University of Hamburg (PhD) under Lambert Schmithausen. He held positions at Leipzig (attested 1995), Vienna (attested 2001), and UC Berkeley as Professor (attested 2011–2026).

Alexander von Staël-Holstein worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After studying at Tartu, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg (Dissertation ~1899–1900), Saint Petersburg, and Harvard, he held posts at Saint Petersburg, Peking University (1918–1929), and Harvard-Yenching Institute (1929), and directed the Sino-Indian Institute (~1927–1937).

Alexandra David-Néel was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at the University of Paris (1887) and Royal Conservatory of Brussels, as well as under Sylvain Lévi, Philippe Édouard Foucaux, Swami Bhaskarananda Saraswati, Kazi Dawa Samdup, and Lachen Gomchen Rinpoche.

Alexandra van der Geer works in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under Karel R. van Kooij, Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, Fabio Martini, John de Vos, and Paul Y. Sondaar, and held a visiting post at the International Institute for Asian Studies.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy (~1815–1832). He served as Professor of Rhetorics at Lycée Charlemagne (~1826–1835), member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1835–1854), and inspector at the Académie de Paris (~1835–1854).

Alexey Belyakov works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed postgraduate studies at Amur State University (2001–2010), later serving as an archaeologist (2007–2013), senior researcher at Amur State University (2013–2017), and associate professor at Heihe University (2017–2018) and Changchun University (2018).
Alexis Cordier was a scholar of Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the École de santé navale (~1890–1894) and earned his Dr.med. at the University of Bordeaux (~1890–1894).

Alexis Sanderson is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Oxford (B.A. 1970) and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He held fellowships at Merton and Brasenose, served as Lecturer and Professor at Oxford (~1977–2015), and became an Emeritus Fellow at All Souls College.

Alf Hiltebeitel was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned a B.A. from Haverford College (1959–1963) and an M.A. and PhD training at the University of Chicago (~1964–1972) under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Victor Turner. He spent his career as a professor at George Washington University (from 1968).
